newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF mulls easing rules on trust fund offers.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF mulls easing rules on trust fund offers.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is considering allowing investment trust management companies to issue trust funds even if fewer than 50 investors subscribe to the offer, a MOF official said on Monday.
Current rules require that at least 50 investors subscribe to an offer for an issue to be made, industry sources say.

However, any decision will depend on an advisory council to the finance minister, which is is currently discussing various ways to deregulate the nation's securities markets and is scheduled to finalise its proposals by the end of June, the official said.
"This issue is one of the topics at the Securities and Exchange Council," the official said.

Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Monday that MOF had decided to scrap the requirement and would also allow domestic investment trusts to contract out fund management to overseas companies.
The ministry plans to seek revisions of the law so that the changes can take place in the 1998/99 year starting in April, it said.
"We expect MOF to change its rules, which will enable investment trust firms to individually design funds for corporate customers," the official said.
